faq.q: Why do we sometimes get two full moons in a month?
faq.a: Full moons come every 29.5 days, a little less than most calendar months. So the full moon drifts earlier through the month, and when one falls on the first day or so, another can fit in at the end.
asks: How can a month have two full moons?

faq.a: Today it usually means the second full moon in a calendar month. Traditionally it meant the third full moon in a season that has four. Either way, it is not blue in colour.
asks: Is a blue moon actually blue?

faq.q: How often does a blue moon happen?
faq.a: About every two to three years, which is why once in a blue moon means rarely. There are about seven monthly blue moons in every 19 years.
asks: What does once in a blue moon mean?

faq.q: Can the Moon really turn blue?
faq.a: Yes, but very rarely. Smoke or ash with particles of just the right size can scatter red light and let blue through, making the Moon look bluish, as happened after the Krakatoa eruption of 1883 and huge Canadian forest fires in 1950.
asks: When did the Moon look blue?

faq.q: Where did the monthly blue moon meaning come from?
faq.a: A 1946 magazine article misread an old almanac's rule about seasons and described a blue moon as the second full moon in a month. The new meaning spread widely after it was used on a radio show in 1980.
asks: Who decided what a blue moon is?

facts: There are about 7 blue moons, by the calendar-month meaning, in every 19 years.
The time from one full moon to the next averages about 29.5 days.
After the Krakatoa eruption in 1883, ash in the air made the Moon look blue in places for months.

quiz.say: Which month can never have a monthly blue moon?
quiz.show: Which month can never have two full moons?
quiz.why: February has only 28 or 29 days, shorter than the 29.5 days between full moons, so it can't fit two.

wrong.1: July has 31 days, enough room for two full moons.
wrong.2: December has 31 days, so it can sometimes hold two full moons.
